solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I don't believe in the possibility of hogging airspace?

definitions.text: I don't believe in the possibility
definitions.meaning: the idiom '...' is said to dismiss something as never going to happen
read literally, hogs (pigs) taking to the air, occupying the sky

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of anyone monopolising the skies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hogging' looks like greedy taking, but it puts hogs, that is pigs, up in the airspace.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a sarcastic retort meaning something is impossible, so it voices disbelief.

clue.text: Reading, putting ring round two references to the Queen?

indicators.note: putting the ring round something places those letters as an outer shell around the rest

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells
R for Regina, and US, the royal 'we' a queen uses of herself

explanation.surface: A reading of documents that wraps a ring round two mentions of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reference is the royal 'we', in the object form US, so R and US sit together inside PEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading through of a text, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Male Hollywood star runs from female Hollywood star

indicators.note: runs are taken away from the actress's name, so 'from' signals removal here

parts.note: Betty Grable, the 1940s pin-up actress
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: One film star's name derived from another's, actor from actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Betty GRABLE loses R to leave Clark GABLE, the leading man of Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a leading man of Hollywood's golden age, a male film star.

clue.text: Blend not entirely unpleasant? That's good to hear

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to meld is to blend together
odious means hateful or unpleasant

explanation.surface: A mixture that is not wholly disagreeable is welcome news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's good to hear' looks like a pleased reply; the last three words define a tuneful sound. MELD loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something melodious is tuneful and pleasant on the ear, sweet-sounding.

clue.text: Heating engineer to show surprise with power cut? A lot getting cut off

indicators.note: the power symbol is cut, removed from the word for showing surprise

parts.note: to gasp is to show surprise
P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: getting cut off means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: many means a lot

explanation.surface: A heating engineer gasps when the power goes off and many customers are disconnected.
explanation.walkthrough: GASP loses P and MANY loses its tail, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasman is a tradesman who installs and services gas boilers and fires.

clue.text: Solution? Metal solution must contain source of same metal

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: must contain means the remedy word holds a letter inside it

parts.note: a cure is a solution to a problem

indicators.note: source of means the first letter, the start of the word

parts.note: the same metal as before, namely tin

explanation.surface: A chemist's query about a metal-based solution containing its own metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'solution' is a remedy, CURE, holding T, the start of TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is a medicine dissolved in alcohol, a type of liquid preparation.

clue.text: Life gutted? Remains in control

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are taken out, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A life emptied out, though the leftovers stay in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is a restraint, and keeping someone on a leash means keeping them under control.

clue.text: Name church advanced around end of Lent

indicators.note: around means the word for advanced is wrapped round a letter

parts.note: risen means gone up, advanced

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A churchy picture: naming at church with Lent ending and Easter approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: To christen is to give a name, originally at baptism.

clue.text: One assessing most of service taken in by military boss

indicators.note: taken in by means the shortened service word sits inside the boss's letters

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rite is a religious service

explanation.surface: An inspector of military service finds much of it absorbed by the general.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic is someone who evaluates and judges, such as a reviewer.

clue.text: Rise about start of breakfast — odd bits of meal missed

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the next word
the odd-placed letters of the meal word are the ones that go
missed says those odd letters are left out, so the even ones stay

explanation.surface: Getting up for breakfast, with bits of the meal skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: MEAL's odd letters, M and A, are missed, leaving E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against authority, as in an uprising.

clue.text: Tabloid article taken into pub reveals devotee of Star?

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: taken into means the article goes inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Reading a tabloid in the pub reveals a fan of the Daily Star, another tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like another newspaper (the Daily Star is a British tabloid), but here it is the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbather devotes time to lying in the sun, our nearest star.

clue.text: Resolute daughter to refuse to eat, with chopped meat in front of her

indicators.note: the meat is placed in front of the daughter, so it comes first
chopped means the meat word has its end cut off

parts.note: steak is meat
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
to fast is to refuse food

explanation.surface: A determined daughter on hunger strike while chopped meat sits before her.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means firm and unwavering, so it shares the sense of determined.

clue.text: Electric current introduced to harbour crane?

indicators.note: introduced to means the current symbol goes inside the harbour word

parts.note: to host is to harbour or accommodate
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A power supply fitted to a dockside crane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' is a verb here, HOST, not a dock; 'crane?' is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A crane is one kind of lifting machine, as a hoist is.

clue.text: Racket returned after line is wound

indicators.note: the reversed racket comes after the line letter
returned means the word for racket is read backwards

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A tennis racket sent back after a line call is a sore point.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is an injury or damaged area of tissue, a wound.

clue.text: Goggles, receiving promise to pay that's deceptive

indicators.note: receiving means the eyewear word takes the debt note inside it

parts.note: specs, spectacles, are a kind of eyewear like goggles
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Eyewear sold on credit with a misleading promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means superficially plausible but actually wrong, so misleading.

clue.text: Very severe, with mother replacing son — striking

indicators.note: replacing means the mother word goes where the son letter was

parts.note: drastic means extreme, very severe
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A family drama: mother takes over from son in a severe and striking change.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic means vivid and arresting, so it is a synonym of striking.

clue.text: Computer graduate pictured?

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
in frame means captured in a picture

explanation.surface: A graduate photographed, perhaps with a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainframe is a large central computer used by organisations.

clue.text: Crazy amateur fliers heading skyward, with Charlie on board

indicators.note: on board means the letter is put inside
in a down clue, heading skyward means read from bottom to top

parts.note: laic means lay, not professional
the RAF is the Royal Air Force
C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Mad amateur pilots climbing with Charlie aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amateur' gives LAIC, the old word for lay; 'heading skyward' turns LAICRAF upward into FARCIAL before 'on board' adds C.
explanation.definitionFit: Farcical means ridiculous or absurd, as crazy can be.

clue.text: Bishop perhaps finding manse's transformed after central heating

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the heating letters

parts.note: CH is the estate-agent abbreviation for central heating

indicators.note: transformed means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleric discovers the vicarage has been made over after heating is installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' wants to be a clergyman with his manse; it is a chess piece. The letters of MANSES are rearranged to give ESSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop is one example of a piece in chess.

clue.text: We will probe company books finding evidence of neglect

indicators.note: will probe means the word goes inside, between the letters

parts.note: B is book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: Auditors promise to investigate a company's accounts and find signs of neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobwebs gather where nobody has cleaned, a sign of neglect.

clue.text: Max coming later perhaps for fish

indicators.note: coming later is the opposite of now, so the clue states the reverse of the answer's second half, as max reverses the first

explanation.surface: Someone called Max is arriving later, maybe to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue, flagged by 'perhaps': read the fish as MIN NOW, the minimum at present, and its natural counterpart is the maximum coming later. 'Max' looks like a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a small freshwater fish, and figuratively an insignificant player.

clue.text: Inclined to scoff about a lot of information in cold weather?

indicators.note: about means the mocking word is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: wry means drily mocking

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: intel is information, especially intelligence

explanation.surface: A cynic sneering at forecasts of cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintery describes conditions typical of winter, cold and bleak.

clue.text: Treatment given to expression of pain: support in bed

parts.note: a pill is a medical treatment
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A patient in bed is given medicine for pain and propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is the cushion that supports the head in bed.

clue.text: Pipe band's opening tune recalled by piper at the end

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word
recalled means the word for tune is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

indicators.note: at the end means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pipe band's first tune is played again by the piper at the close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' looks like the bagpipes; it is a tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A briar is a tobacco pipe made from the root of the briar heath.

clue.text: Show Minister getting one-third of Europe upset

parts.note: Rev, Reverend, is the title of a minister

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read upwards
one-third of a six-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A government minister upset by a third of Europe makes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a government minister; it is a clergyman, REV. EU is reversed to UE.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical entertainment of sketches and songs, a type of show.

clue.text: Unfortunately hit in face or head

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unlucky blow to the face or head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like part of the body after 'face'; it is a leader. HIT IN FACE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head or leader of a clan or tribe.

clue.text: Supplier of fake news mostly under cover of a second fake name

indicators.note: under cover of means placed inside, covered by the outer letters
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a liar supplies falsehoods

explanation.surface: A disinformation peddler working undercover with a false identity.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name used to hide identity.

clue.text: Stop wasting time in US city bay, backsliding, uncertain

indicators.note: in means the shortened stop word goes inside
backsliding means the city and bay words are read backwards

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a cove is a small bay

indicators.note: wasting means a letter is lost

parts.note: to quit is to stop

explanation.surface: Someone dithering over whether to leave a bay in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' reverses only the city and bay, giving EVOCAL; 'wasting' drops T to leave QUI, which goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivocal means ambiguous or open to doubt, so unsure in outcome.

clue.text: Blazing footballers returned anger

indicators.note: returned means the footballers' letters are read backwards

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Footballers came back hot with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire means on fire, alight, burning.

clue.text: Sporting award highlighting the "cow"' in "coward"?

definitions.meaning: worn by the overall leader of the Tour de France
a coward is yellow and a cow may be a Jersey

explanation.surface: A quirky wordplay commentary on the 'cow' found inside the word 'coward'.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow means cowardly; a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow from the Channel Island of Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow jersey is the cycling prize awarded to the Tour de France leader.
